'''Francis Kofi Ampenyin Allotey''' {{post-nominals|country=GHA|FGA|[[African Academy of Sciences|FAAS]]|OV}} (9 August 1932<ref>{{Cite book |date=2007 |title=African Doctorates in Mathematics: A Catalogue |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wgiTQUcE21UC&dq=Francis+Kofi+Allotey+1932&pg=PA128 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171103175415/https://books.google.com/books?id=wgiTQUcE21UC&pg=PA128&dq=Francis+Kofi+Allotey+1932&hl=en&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwiwxsjMtqLXAhXnJsAKHSn3AnAQ6AEIJDAA#v=onepage&q=Francis%20Kofi%20Allotey%201932&f=false |archive-date=3 November 2017 |access-date=19 May 2024 |publisher=Lulu.com |isbn=978-1-4303-1867-5 }}</ref><ref name=":3">{{cite web|url=http://publications.uew.edu.gh/2015/hof/prof-f-k-ampenyin-allotey|title=Hall of Fame|access-date=4 November 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171103175417/http://publications.uew.edu.gh/2015/hof/prof-f-k-ampenyin-allotey|archive-date=3 November 2017}}</ref> – 2 November 2017<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=Renowned Ghanaian mathematician Prof Francis Allotey dies at 85 |url=https://www.graphic.com.gh/news/general-news/renowned-ghanaian-mathematician-prof-francis-allotey-dies-at-85.html |location=Accra, Ghana|access-date=2023-05-05 |newspaper=[[Daily Graphic (Ghana)|Daily Graphic]]|date=3 November 2017 |language=en-gb}}</ref>) was a [[Ghana]]ian [[Mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.graphic.com.gh/news/general-news/carry-on-torch-lit-by-prof-francis-allotey-prez-urges-ghanaians.html|location=Accra, Ghana|title=Carry on torch lit by Prof. Francis Allotey - Prez urges Ghanaians|author=Daily Graphic|newspaper=[[Daily Graphic (Ghana)|Daily Graphic]]|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-02-24|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180224165442/https://www.graphic.com.gh/news/general-news/carry-on-torch-lit-by-prof-francis-allotey-prez-urges-ghanaians.html|archive-date=24 February 2018|df=dmy-all|date=24 February 2018}}</ref><ref name=":8">{{Cite news|url=https://www.graphic.com.gh/features/features/the-great-mathematician-and-scientist-in-memoriam-to-a-native-of-saltpond-a-son-of-ghana-and-a-citizen-of-the-world.html|location=Accra, Ghana|title=Professor Allotey: The great mathematician and scientist|author=Daily Graphic|newspaper=[[Daily Graphic (Ghana)|Daily Graphic]]|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-02-24|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180223172924/https://www.graphic.com.gh/features/features/the-great-mathematician-and-scientist-in-memoriam-to-a-native-of-saltpond-a-son-of-ghana-and-a-citizen-of-the-world.html|archive-date=23 February 2018|df=dmy-all|date=23 February 2018}}</ref> Together with [[Daniel Afedzi Akyeampong]], he became the first Ghanaian to obtain a doctorate in mathematical sciences, earned in 1966.

==Early life and education==
Allotey was born on 9 August 1932 in the [[Fante people|Fante]] town of [[Saltpond]] in the [[Central Region (Ghana)|Central Region]] of [[Ghana]] to Joseph Kofi Allotey, a general commodities [[merchant]] and Alice Esi Nyena Allotey, a [[dressmaker]] from the Royal Dehyena family of Enyan Owomase and Ekumfi Edumafa, in the [[Central Region (Ghana)|Central Region]] of Ghana.<ref name=":4">{{cite web|url=http://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/people/pop-up.php?ID=136|title=Professor Francis Kofi Ampenyi Allotey |work=ghanaweb.com|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070415123500/http://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/people/pop-up.php?ID=136|archive-date=15 April 2007}}</ref><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/In-memoriam-of-the-great-mathematician-and-scientist-Prof-Allotey-628389|title=In memoriam of the great mathematician and scientist; Prof. Allotey|website=www.ghanaweb.com|date=22 February 2018 |language=en|access-date=2018-02-24|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180222130200/https://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/In-memoriam-of-the-great-mathematician-and-scientist-Prof-Allotey-628389|archive-date=22 February 2018|df=dmy-all}}</ref> His father owned a [[bookstore]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":6" /> During his childhood,  Allotey spent his free time in his father's [[bookstore]] reading the biographies of famous scientists which piqued his interest in science.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":6" /> He was raised a [[Catholic Church|Roman Catholic]].<ref name=":6" /> He had his primary education at St. John the Baptist Catholic (Boys) School in Saltpond and was among the pioneer batch of [[Ghana National College]] when the school was founded in July 1948 by [[Kwame Nkrumah]].<ref name=":1" />

After secondary school, he attended the University Tutorial College in Ghana and the [[London South Bank University|London Borough Polytechnic]].<ref name=":7">{{Cite web|url=http://wwwf.imperial.ac.uk/~ruzh/papers/Allotey.pdf|title=Francis Allotey Biography|last=Imperial College London|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180224165438/http://wwwf.imperial.ac.uk/~ruzh/papers/Allotey.pdf|archive-date=24 February 2018|df=dmy-all}}</ref> He held master's and doctorate degrees from [[Princeton University]], awarded in 1966 and earlier the [[Diploma of Imperial College]], obtained in 1960.<ref name=":5">{{cite web|date=27 May 1997|publisher=buffalo.edu|website=Physicists of the African Diaspora|title=Francis Kofi Ampenyin Allotey|access-date=22 March 2015|url=http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/physics/allotey_franciska.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150406015635/http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/physics/allotey_franciska.html|archive-date=6 April 2015}}</ref><ref name=iop>{{cite web|publisher=IOP [[Institute of Physics]]|title=Honorary fellows: Professor Francis Kofi Ampenyin Allotey - African Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Ghana|access-date=22 March 2015|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/hon_fellowship/hon_fellows/page_56407.html}}</ref> He was tutored by the Pakistani Nobel prize-winning physicist [[Abdus Salam]] as an undergraduate at Imperial College.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iop.org/about/obituaries/page_72192.html#gref|title=Francis Kofi Allotey (1932–2017)|website=www.iop.org|access-date=2019-11-25}}{{Dead link|date=February 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> During his time at Princeton, Allotey was mentored by many physicists such as [[Robert H. Dicke|Robert Dicke]], [[Val Logsdon Fitch|Val Fitch]], [[J. Robert Oppenheimer|Robert Oppenheimer]], [[Paul Dirac|Paul A. M. Dirac]] and [[Chen-Ning Yang|C. N. Yang]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

==Career==
He was known for the "''Allotey Formalism''" which arose from his work on [[soft X-ray]] [[spectroscopy]]. He was the 1973 recipient of the ''UK Prince Philip Golden Award'' for his work in this area.<ref name=":7" /> A founding fellow of the [[African Academy of Sciences]],<ref>[[Paulus Gerdes|Gerdes, Paulus]] (2007)
[https://books.google.com/books?id=wgiTQUcE21UC&pg=PA370 ''African Doctorates in Mathematics''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171103175415/https://books.google.com/books?id=wgiTQUcE21UC&pg=PA370|date=3 November 2017}}, p. 370. Commission on the History of Mathematics in Africa</ref> in 1974, he became the first Ghanaian full professor of mathematics and head of the Department of Mathematics and later Dean of the Faculty of Science at the [[Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology]].<ref>''[[New African]]'' (January 2007).  [http://goliath.ecnext.com/coms2/gi_0199-6161953/The-Allotey-formalism-the-man.html "The Allotey formalism: the man who formulated the technique used to determine matter in outer space, Professor Francis K.A. Allotey, receives the 2006 Black S/heroes Award"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090801070920/http://goliath.ecnext.com/coms2/gi_0199-6161953/The-Allotey-formalism-the-man.html|date=1 August 2009}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://citifmonline.com/2018/02/23/state-funeral-held-for-prof-allotey-photos/|title=State funeral held for Prof. Allotey [Photos]  |date=2018-02-23|work=Ghana News|access-date=2018-02-23|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180223194341/https://citifmonline.com/2018/02/23/state-funeral-held-for-prof-allotey-photos/|archive-date=2018-02-23}}</ref> He was also the founding director of the [[Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology|KNUST]] Computer Centre before he assumed his position as the Pro-Vice-Chancellor of the university.<ref name=":1" /> Among Allotey's colleagues on the mathematics faculty at KNUST was Atu Mensa Taylor (died in 1977), the third Ghanaian to obtain a doctorate in mathematics.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Atu Mensa Taylor - Mathematician of the African Diaspora|url=http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/taylor_atumensa.html|access-date=2020-10-30|website=www.math.buffalo.edu}}</ref> Taylor had received his DPhil (1967) from [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] under the Welsh mathematical physicist, [[John Trevor Lewis]], having also received an MA there many years before.<ref name=":2" />

Allotey was the President of the [[Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and a member of a number of international scientific organizations including the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics|Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] Scientific Council since 1996.<ref name=":1" /> He was also the President of the Ghana Institute of Physics and the founding President of the African Physical Society.<ref name=":1" /> He was instrumental in getting Ghana to join the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]], making it one of the first few African countries to join the Union. He collaborated with the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics|IUPAP]] and [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics|ICTP]] to encourage [[physics education]] in developing countries through workshops and conferences in order to create awareness on the continent.<ref name=":1" />

Allotey was the Chairman of Board of Trustees of the [[Accra Institute of Technology]], the President of the [[African Institute for Mathematical Sciences#AIMS Ghana|African Institute for Mathematical Sciences, Ghana]]. He was an honorary fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref name=iop/>  He was an honorary Fellow of the Nigerian Mathematical Society among others.<ref name=":1" /> He consulted for many international institutions such as the [[UNESCO]], [[International Atomic Energy Agency|IAEA]] and [[United Nations Industrial Development Organization|UNIDO]].<ref name=":1" /> He was also the Vice president, 7th General Assembly of [[Intergovernmental Bureau for Informatics|Intergovernmental Bureau of Informatics]] (IBI).<ref name=":7" /> He was also instrumental in the advancement of [[computer education]] in Africa and worked closely with organisations such as the [[IBM|IBM International]] and the International Federation for Information Processing.<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /> In 2004, he was the only African among the 100 most eminent physicists and mathematicians in the world to be cited in a book titled, "''One hundred reasons to be a scientist''."<ref name=":1" />

The Professor Francis Allotey Graduate School was established in 2009 at the [[Accra Institute of Technology]].<ref>
Ani-Awukubea, Regina (21 January 2009) [http://www.thestatesmanonline.com/pages/news_detail.php?section=1&newsid=8056 "The AIT commences Open University programme"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111109193250/http://thestatesmanonline.com/pages/news_detail.php?section=1&newsid=8056 |date=9 November 2011 }}  . ''The Statesman'' (Ghana); accessed 4 November 2017.
</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ghanabusinessnews.com/2017/11/03/prof-francis-allotey-dies|title=Prof. Francis Allotey dies|website=Ghana Business News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171103175415/https://www.ghanabusinessnews.com/2017/11/03/prof-francis-allotey-dies|first=Emmanuel K.|last= Dogbevi|archive-date=3 November 2017|url-status=live|access-date=4 November 2017|date=3 November 2017}}</ref> The institute provides master's degrees in [[Business administration|Business Administration]] and [[Software engineering|Software Engineering]] and doctoral programmes in Information Technology and Philosophy.<ref name=":1" /> The [[Government of Ghana]] awarded him the Millennium Excellence Award in 2005, and dedicated a [[postage stamp]] in his honour. In 2009 he received the [[Order of the Volta]] and was posthumously awarded the ''Osagyefo Kwame Nkrumah African Genius Award'' in 2017.<ref name=":1" /> He helped establish the African Institute of Mathematical Sciences in Ghana in 2012.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

== Personal life ==
Allotey first married Edoris Enid Chandler from [[Barbados]], whom he met while they were both studying in [[London]].<ref name=":8" /> They had two children, Francis Kojo Enu Allotey and Joseph Kobina Nyansa Allotey. Chandler died in November 1981. He then remarried to Ruby Asie Mirekuwa Akuamoah.<ref name=":8" /> Together they raised her two children, Cilinnie and Kay. Akuamoah died in October, 2011. Overall, Allotey had four children and 20 grandchildren.<ref name=":8" />

== Death and state funeral ==
Francis Allotey died of [[Death by natural causes|natural causes]] on 2 November 2017.<ref name=":0" /> The Ghanaian government accorded him a [[state funeral]] in recognition of his contributions to the advancement of science and technology in Ghana.<ref name=":1" />  His body was interred in his hometown, [[Saltpond]], Central Region.<ref name=":1" />
